proposed_widenings.name: grant_illusion_awareness
proposed_widenings.justification: When a creature passes the Investigation check against a silent image (or any illusion), it 'can see through the image.' This is a persistent per-creature state change — the creature's relationship to the illusion is updated — that has no EffectAtom. { kind: 'none' } was used as a placeholder for onPass in the ability_check_gate, leaving the disbelief outcome unmodeled. The create_illusion atom comment explicitly defers this to 'separate surfaces'; that separate surface needs an atom.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the creature can see through the image.

notes: Three operations encode cleanly: (1) passive → create_illusion (visual, huge), (2) on_caster_spends_action (Magic) → reposition_attachment, (3) on_creature_studies → ability_check_gate (Int vs spell DC). Typecheck passes, tracer runs without errors. The only gap is the disbelief outcome: onPass uses { kind: 'none' } because no atom models 'creature can see through illusion.' The create_illusion atom comment acknowledges this deferral explicitly. The `caster_recasts_spell` earlyEnd trigger is listed in types.ts for Silent Image but absent from the provided source text entries; omitted pending SRD passage confirmation.
